instruction: After attempting "jenv version" in terminal, I got "jenv: command not found". Please help me solve this issue so jenv commands work right away.

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

metadata.explanation: Task requires fixing 'jenv: command not found' by adding jenv initialization to ~/.bashrc. Evaluator checks if 'jenv init' is present in .bashrc, which indicates jenv has been properly configured. Similar pattern to original conda task.
metadata.verification_notes: Used existing exact_match metric and vm_command_line getter. Checked for 'jenv init' in .bashrc which is the standard jenv configuration pattern.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete verification: Only checks if string 'jenv init' exists in .bashrc, not whether jenv commands actually work
Wrong verification approach: Instruction says 'so jenv commands work right away' but evaluator doesn't test if 'jenv version' command succeeds
Loose pattern matching: grep pattern 'jenv init' is too permissive - could match comments like '# TODO: add jenv init' or incorrect syntax
Missing functional verification: Should test that 'jenv version' no longer returns 'command not found', rather than just checking config file content
Incomplete configuration check: Even if 'jenv init' is in .bashrc, jenv might not be installed or in PATH, so commands still won't work
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Better approach: Test actual functionality by running 'jenv version' and verifying it doesn't output 'command not found'
Alternative: Check for the complete proper init line using: grep -q 'eval "$(jenv init -)"' ~/.bashrc
Comprehensive test: Run 'source ~/.bashrc && jenv version' to verify both configuration and functionality
Multi-step verification: Check (1) jenv is installed, (2) proper init line in .bashrc with correct syntax, (3) jenv commands work
